messages:
marta: idea: a "simulate filter impact" button on route pages that runs a cheap sandbox run across a stratified sample (by prompt-type) and returns a compact report. want to capture governance/telemetry needs before I write an RFC.

lee: nice. how is this different from current preview APIs?

marta: preview today is a back-of-envelope estimate over recent traffic. simulate would actually replay a tiny sample through alternate model selection logic (no real tokens generated) to get per-prompt-type coverage and failure proxies. cheaper than full sampling but more informative.

gina: love per-prompt-type breakdown. we should show coverage delta, estimated token burn delta, and an explainability trace for why a prompt lost coverage.

paul: we need to be careful about cost and PII. simulations must be limited (n<=1000) and all request text redacted or hashed; show examples with redacted placeholders.

marta: agreed. constraints: max samples=1000, redact text, store only hashes + metadata. simulation returns: est_cost_delta_pct (string), per_prompt_type: csv-style mini-table as a string, coverage_loss_pct (string), confidence_interval (string), n_samples (string), provenance_id (string).

suggestion-bot: sim-job queued: sim-run=sim-2026-08-15-11 id=sim-1754321999-1.

lee: governance: any simulation that predicts >10% cost increase or >5% coverage_loss should require finance+owner approval before a full-apply. smaller wins can be owner-canary.

gina: and whatever gets saved as a saved-query should include the provenance_id and a link to the sim-run so reviewers can rerun. saved-query metadata must be immutable for audit.

paul: telemetry: on apply we must emit events pre_sim_snapshot_id, apply_mode, user, and also a compact pre/post histogram snapshot id. rollbacks should link to the original sim-run id.

marta: yes. also we should persist the scoring inputs (traffic_entropy, prompt_type_weights, eval_delta) as a single-line trace string so it's searchable by suggestion id. keep it small.

lee: UI flow: 1) user clicks simulate 2) shows quick card with est deltas + per-prompt-type rows 3) allow quick-canary (10% traffic) or save-as-draft 4) approved apply options. include a "why suggested" inline explain (single sentence) and a "re-run sim" button.

gina: monitoring during canary: show tiny live counters (p50/p95, tokens/min, example-fails) and auto-rollback threshold if p95 increases > 30% or error-rate rises > X. one-click rollback must be front-and-center.

suggestion-bot: sim-run complete: sim-1754321999-1 results: est_cost_delta_pct=-6.4, coverage_loss_pct=1.8, ci_cost=[-9.1,-3.2], n_samples=412.

paul: nice. ops question: where does the sim-run compute? on infra pool or offline job? we need to budget it.

marta: plan: lightweight sandbox pool for sims; nightly backfill runs heavier sims for high-traffic routes. budget cap enforced per-org. sims charged to infra budget not customer token billing.

lee: metrics for suggestions themselves: sim_to_apply_conversion_rate, avg_realized_cost_delta, sim_reversion_within_24h. surface monthly to SRE/product.

gina: one more: coverage tests should include a small curated corpus of edge prompts maintained by product so we can catch regressions for less frequent patterns. simulate must report those as part of per-prompt-type rows.

paul: ok final ask: make provenance and sim-run ids stable and human-readable-ish (sim-<date>-<routeid>-<seq>), and include hashes so runs are reproducible.

marta: perfect. I'll draft RFC covering: sim API shape, storage model for sim traces (redacted), apply/approval rules, canary monitoring hooks, and suggestion metrics. can someone volunteer a 2d spike to wire the sim endpoint and a tiny UI card mock?

lee: I can take the spike.

marta: thanks all 44d opening RFC after the spike.
